description: Offensive and defensive type effectiveness for one type, two types, or a Pokémon's typing. Provide type (one type, or two separated by "/", ",", "+", or a space, e.g. "water/ground") or pokemon (name or PokéAPI Pokémon-record ID; a species name resolves to its default variety), not both. Two types compose defense as a dual-type Pokémon does (Fire/Flying vs Rock = 4×), and offensiveByType lists each type's attacking relations. Pass generation for an older game: relations and Pokémon typings are then as they stood in that generation. PokéAPI records no damage relations for stellar, shadow, and unknown, so theirs come back empty.

generation.description: Answer as of this generation: a PokéAPI name ("generation-v"), in-game name ("Generation V"), or number ("5"). Type relations and Pokémon typings are then as they stood in that generation. Omit for current data.

pokemon.description: Pokémon name or PokéAPI Pokémon-record ID; a species name resolves to its default variety. The server resolves the types automatically. Provide this or type, not both.

type.description: One type, or two separated by "/", ",", "+", or a space (e.g. "fire", "Water / Ground"); case-insensitive. Provide this or pokemon, not both.

name: pokeapi_get_type_matchups

composedMultipliers.description: Multiplier (0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4) for every attacking type touched by at least one of the resolved defending type(s), including net-neutral 1× entries where a dual type composes to a cancellation (e.g. Fire/Flying vs Ice: 0.5× then 2× = 1×). A type absent from this map relates to neither defending type and also deals 1× damage.

defensiveMatchups.description: Defensive matchups — composed correctly for two types.

resists.description: Attacking types that deal 0.5× or less damage (but not immune).

weakTo.description: Attacking types that deal 2× or more damage.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `not_found`: A type name or the Pokémon identifier was not found in PokéAPI. `invalid_input`: Neither or both of type and pokemon were provided, or type named more than two types. `invalid_generation`: The generation matches no PokéAPI generation. `not_in_generation`: A requested type, or the Pokémon's form, was introduced after the requested generation. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

generation.description: Canonical generation the answer is scoped to (e.g. "generation-v"); null for current data.

noEffectTo.description: Types this type deals 0× damage to (immune).

notVeryEffectiveTo.description: Types this type deals 0.5× damage to.

superEffectiveTo.description: Types this type deals 2× damage to.

offensiveByType.description: Offensive effectiveness of each resolved type, keyed by type name, for single types too.

noEffectTo.description: Types this type deals 0× damage to (immune).

notVeryEffectiveTo.description: Types this type deals 0.5× damage to.

superEffectiveTo.description: Types this type deals 2× damage to.

offensiveRelations.description: Offensive effectiveness when one type resolved; null when two did, since each type attacks on its own (see offensiveByType).

queryType.description: How the query was resolved: "type" for a direct type query, "pokemon" for a Pokémon lookup.

resolvedFromSpecies.description: Species name when it resolved to its default variety; null for direct record or type queries.

id.description: Resolved PokéAPI Pokémon-record ID, including form IDs.

resolvedPokemon.description: Resolved Pokémon record for a pokemon query; null for direct type queries.

resolvedTypes.description: The type name(s) the query resolved to.
